title: Temporary-directory retention follows the owning Jupiter test’s outcome
summary: The successful Jupiter owner’s temporary directory disappeared even after a sibling failed. Reversing their order left only the failed owner’s marker after launcher completion.

change.description: Jupiter now scopes recorded child failures to their own extension context, so an earlier failure does not prevent an unrelated successful test’s ON_SUCCESS temporary directory from being cleaned up.

notes: An independently successful owner’s cleanup policy does not depend on whether a sibling has already failed. Files.exists is an observation outside the test engine.

The intermediate commit f7f1d51d4c57 changed only release notes. Its junit-jupiter-engine/src/main tree (bf0e7ee77cdfc878a8075699153823292105238e) is identical to the parent’s. The second commit changed that production tree.
With identical compiled caller bytes, 5.12.1 matched the parent and 5.12.2 matched the landing on all three histories.
